framework.method: Aider Polyglot benchmark: full-file edits, official pytest suites, up to two attempts

goal: Implement the requested code edit correctly. Respect the supplied API and constraints. Use observed test results as evidence. Prefer lower cost only among approaches that meet the task requirements.
notes: 34 official coding exercises: 10 disjoint learning cases and 24 held-out scenarios.
Use upstream instructions, solution skeleton and tests without authored cases.
Aider two-attempt test-and-repair method; transport through Cynosure is an adaptation, not the unmodified Aider leaderboard harness.
Never expose reference implementation or test source to model; test error output is allowed only after execution.
Each heldout Cynosure task uses its own copy of a frozen experience snapshot.
All providers use the same prompts, output limits and official tests.
OS-sandboxed execution, no network or credentials.
No model is assigned a prior quality score. Strong-model differences include success, repair, price and latency.

Generation requests use262144 tokens except documented provider output ceilings: GLM5.3 and Flash131072. Delivery-first Jev; Grok fallback on uncertainty or decision failure. Evaluations remain observations, never delivery gates.
